stem: A mixture of $6$ g of hydrogen and $32$ g of oxygen has a total pressure of $20$ atm. Find the partial pressure of oxygen, assuming ideal behaviour. Take $M(\text{H}_2)=2\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$ and $M(\text{O}_2)=32\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.
working:
$n_{\text{H}_2}=\dfrac{6}{2}=3\ \text{mol}$, $n_{\text{O}_2}=\dfrac{32}{32}=1\ \text{mol}$
$x_{\text{O}_2}=\dfrac{1}{3+1}=\dfrac{1}{4}$
$p_{\text{O}_2}=x_{\text{O}_2}P_{\text{total}}=\dfrac{1}{4}\times20=5\ \text{atm}$

Independent check: n(H₂)=6/2=3 mol; n(O₂)=32/32=1 mol. Thus P(O₂)=(1/4)(20)=5 atm.
solution:
The partial pressure is the mole fraction multiplied by the total pressure. The amounts are $n_{\text{H}_2}=6/2=3$ mol and $n_{\text{O}_2}=32/32=1$ mol.
$$p_{\text{O}_2}=\frac{1}{3+1}\times20=5\ \text{atm}$$
